intent: Decide whether forwarding this author's work for technical scrutiny would be worth the risk.
context: A weary hiring manager has reviewed many polished agentic-engineering portfolios; three promising links were dismissed by the architect.
desired_outcome: Enough legible, attributable evidence to make a confident forward-or-decline decision.
engagement_cues: A short path from professional claim to inspectable decision, responsibility and consequence.
friction_cues: Another fluent pitch that makes the manager risk looking foolish when a technical peer opens the link.
name: Hiring evaluator
invariants: Assesses whether evidence supports the professional claims being made.
Considers the reputational cost of forwarding work that fails later scrutiny.

variation_axes.description: The reader’s role in deciding whether work advances.

values.description: Screens for relevance and clear evidence.
Decides whether a candidate merits team time.
Risks personal credibility when recommending the work.

variation_axes.description: How much inspectable detail the reader needs before making a recommendation.

values.description: Needs concrete evidence for each major claim.
Needs to inspect decisions and trade-offs.
Needs evidence likely to survive technical questioning.

intent: Strip the presentation away and test whether this author understands the engineering underneath.
context: A principal engineer or architect has already dismissed three similar forwarded portfolios and expects pattern vocabulary to conceal thin reasoning.
desired_outcome: A technical account that survives questions about mechanism, alternatives, cost, evidence and limits—or reveals where it does not.
engagement_cues: Specific decisions and falsifiable detail that remain coherent under hostile scrutiny.
friction_cues: Named patterns, polished diagrams or confident outcomes that collapse when asked why this approach was chosen.
name: Jaded architect
invariants: Tests engineering claims beneath the presentation and pattern vocabulary.
Looks for mechanisms, alternatives, costs, evidence, and limits that withstand scrutiny.

variation_axes.description: Which engineering concern most shapes the reader’s scrutiny.

values.description: Implementation choices and evidence of execution.

variation_axes.description: How the reader approaches a claim that sounds polished.

values.description: Asks how the result was produced.
Asks what else was considered and why rejected.
Looks for evidence that could disprove the claim.

intent: Imagine solving a difficult problem alongside this author.
context: Could become a colleague or partner and cares about how disagreement and credit are handled.
desired_outcome: A sense that the author can reason openly, change course and make others effective.
engagement_cues: Candid uncertainty, colleagues' contributions and decisions made with rather than over people.
friction_cues: Blame shifted onto absent teammates or a flawless-protagonist story.
name: Prospective collaborator
invariants: Imagines working through a difficult problem with the author.
Values open reasoning, fair credit, disagreement, and shared effectiveness.

variation_axes.description: The kind of working relationship the reader imagines.

values.description: A partner depending on delivered work.

variation_axes.description: What most helps the reader judge whether collaboration would work.

values.description: Evidence the author can change course.
